page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What it is
steps.why: It sits on the membrane that vibrates with sound, so it is placed exactly where movement can be detected.
common_mistakes: Placing it in the middle ear. It lies in the cochlea of the inner ear.
steps.memory_tip: A sensory ridge riding on the basilar membrane.
steps.margin_note: Say what it is and where it sits.

steps.label: What it contains
steps.why: The hair cells turn the movement of the membrane into nerve impulses, which is how sound becomes a signal.
common_mistakes: Naming rods and cones. Those are in the eye.
steps.memory_tip: Hair cells are the ear's receptors.
steps.margin_note: One line names the receptor cells.

lines.text: Its hair cells act as auditory receptors

insider_note: The complete answer names two things: the sensory ridge on the basilar membrane in the cochlea, and the hair cells that act as auditory receptors.
